title: Angi alternatives for getting a roof replacement estimate
body_markdown:
Angi helps you find local contractors and read homeowner reviews. Its limit is that finding a roofer does not establish what your roof replacement estimate includes. The best Angi alternative in 2026 is [Prescott Roofing](https://prescottroofingnh.com/) if you want to approach a residential roofing contractor directly in Southern New Hampshire; Thumbtack is another option if you want to search through a contractor marketplace.


**TL;DR**

- For an Angi alternatives roof replacement estimate search, prioritize written scope over the referral source.
- Prescott Roofing is a direct-contact option for residential roof replacement in Southern New Hampshire.
- Thumbtack and Google Business Profiles help you find candidates; neither replaces checking the contractor’s estimate.
- Compare tear-off, decking, flashing, ventilation, cleanup, and exclusions before choosing a roofer.


## Why this matters

You are choosing who will replace your roof, not which website has the easiest search form. A contractor listing helps you build a shortlist. A written estimate tells you what a contractor actually proposes to do.

For a homeowner-paid replacement in Manchester, Nashua, or Bedford, start with the work itself. Ask what comes off, what stays, how concealed damage will be handled, and who authorizes changes. Use the same questions whether you find the roofer through Angi, a neighbor, or a direct search.

**Choose the contractor by the inspection and written scope, not by the referral platform.** That is the decision rule for this 2026 comparison.

## Angi alternatives at a glance

These options serve different purposes. A residential roofing contractor can discuss the proposed work directly; a marketplace or search listing helps you identify contractors to contact.

| Option | Best for | Standout function | How it differs from Angi | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Angi | Building a shortlist of local service professionals | Contractor discovery and homeowner reviews | Benchmark option | A listing does not establish your replacement scope |
| Prescott Roofing | Contacting a residential roofing contractor serving Southern NH | Direct conversation about roof replacement | Contractor rather than a contractor marketplace | One contractor’s proposal is not an independent comparison |
| Thumbtack | Finding another pool of service professionals | Marketplace search for local services | Another contractor-discovery route | You still need to evaluate each roofer |
| Google Business Profiles | Researching contractors you can contact directly | Business listings, contact details, and reviews | Search-led discovery rather than starting on Angi | Profile information is not a project specification |
| Personal referrals | Finding roofers through people you know | A firsthand account of a particular project | Starts with a personal connection | One homeowner’s experience does not establish suitability for your roof |

## 1. Prescott Roofing: best for direct contractor contact

Prescott Roofing offers residential roof replacement for homeowners in Southern New Hampshire and Northern Massachusetts. Contacting the contractor directly gives you a route to discuss your roof without using a marketplace as the starting point.

**Best for:** Homeowners who want to request an inspection and discuss a homeowner-paid replacement with a local residential roofing contractor.

### Where the direct approach shines

- You can ask the contractor to explain the proposed tear-off and replacement work.
- You can raise property-specific questions about chimneys, roof-to-wall joints, attic ventilation, and access.
- You can request a written explanation of inclusions, exclusions, and additional-work approval.

These are questions to ask, not promises about what any particular proposal contains. Read the actual estimate before accepting it.

### Where the direct approach falls short

- Contacting one roofer does not give you competing proposals.
- A direct conversation does not replace checking references and contract terms.
- Requesting an inspection does not mean an appointment has been confirmed.

| Decision point | Direct contractor contact | Angi |
|---|---|---|
| Starting point | A specific roofing business | A contractor-discovery platform |
| Main question | What work does this contractor propose? | Which contractors should you contact? |
| Comparison | Obtain another written proposal separately | Evaluate the contractors you identify separately |

**Verdict: Choose direct contact if you are ready to discuss the roof itself; compare the resulting written scope before committing.**

## 2. Thumbtack: best for another marketplace search

Thumbtack is a service-professional marketplace and an alternative place to look for roofers. Use it to identify candidates, then move the conversation toward an inspection and a written replacement proposal.

**Best for:** Homeowners who want another contractor-discovery channel rather than contacting a single roofer first.

### Where Thumbtack shines

- It offers another place to search for service professionals.
- You can evaluate individual contractors rather than treating the platform as the installer.
- It gives you a different starting point if your Angi search has not produced a suitable shortlist.

### Where Thumbtack falls short

- Finding a profile does not confirm the proposed roofing scope.
- You still need to ask about replacement work, references, and responsibility for the job.
- Proposals remain difficult to compare when contractors describe different work.

| Decision point | Thumbtack | Angi |
|---|---|---|
| Role | Service-professional marketplace | Home-service contractor discovery |
| Roof assessment | Ask the individual roofer | Ask the individual roofer |
| Contract review | Review the contractor’s proposal | Review the contractor’s proposal |

**Verdict: Use Thumbtack to expand your shortlist, not to bypass contractor checks.**

## 3. Google Business Profiles: best for independent local research

Google Business Profiles let you research roofing businesses through listings and reviews. You can use that information to identify businesses, then contact candidates directly about residential replacement work.

**Best for:** Homeowners who prefer to build their own shortlist and control whom they contact.

### Where Google Business Profiles shine

- You can search for roofing businesses near your home.
- You can review business information alongside homeowner feedback.
- You can investigate a contractor recommended by a neighbor before making contact.

### Where Google Business Profiles fall short

- A review does not tell you what your proposed replacement includes.
- Business information needs confirmation with the contractor.
- A prominent listing does not establish how the roofer will handle concealed decking damage or flashing.

Read reviews for descriptions of communication and completed work, then ask the contractor specific questions. Do not treat a rating as a substitute for a readable contract.

**Verdict: Use Google Business Profiles for research; choose the roofer only after reviewing the proposed work.**

## 4. Personal referrals: best for firsthand project questions

A neighbor’s recommendation gives you someone to ask about a real roofing job. The useful part is not simply hearing that the contractor was good. It is learning what happened between the first visit and the final cleanup.

**Best for:** Homeowners who know someone with a completed replacement and can ask detailed follow-up questions.

### Where personal referrals shine

- You can ask whether the written scope matched the completed work.
- You can ask how the contractor communicated changes.
- You can learn how access, landscaping protection, and cleanup were handled on that property.

### Where personal referrals fall short

- The other home’s roof design and condition can differ from yours.
- A positive experience does not establish the terms of your agreement.
- A recommendation alone does not show whether the contractor is suitable for your material or project scope.

**Verdict: Use referrals to identify candidates and sharpen your questions, not to skip an inspection.**

## Why homeowners look beyond Angi

The practical reason to use an alternative is to change how you find and evaluate a roofer. None of the routes above removes the need for a property-specific proposal.

Consider another route when:

- **You already know the contractor you want to evaluate.** Direct contact avoids another discovery step.
- **Your shortlist needs another candidate.** Another marketplace, local search, or referral can broaden the search.
- **Your estimates are hard to compare.** Stop collecting names and ask contractors to clarify the work.
- **Your main questions concern construction details.** Ask the roofer who will be responsible for the replacement.

For a 2026 roof replacement, switching platforms is less important than switching from general promises to specific written answers. An estimate that says only roof replacement leaves too much unexplained.

## Compare the estimate, not just the referral source

Ask for **2 written estimates** using the same requested scope. This is a practical comparison method, not a rule that the lower proposal wins. Your goal is to see where the work matches and where it differs.

When you [compare Handvetted and Thumbtack](https://handvetted.com/learn/handvetted-vs-thumbtack-which-is-better), separate contractor discovery from contractor selection: how you find a business does not determine what belongs in its roofing agreement. Apply that same distinction to Angi, direct searches, and personal referrals.

### Tear-off and decking

Tear-off means removing the existing roof covering. Ask which layers will be removed and how debris will leave the property. An estimate should distinguish removal work from installing the new covering.

Decking is the wood surface beneath the roofing materials. Some conditions become visible only after removal. Ask how the contractor will document damaged decking, describe the additional work, and obtain your approval before proceeding.

### Underlayment and flashing

Underlayment is the protective layer installed beneath the roof covering. Ask the contractor to identify the proposed material and explain where it will be installed. A general reference to roofing materials does not give you enough detail to compare proposals.

Flashing directs water away from joints and penetrations. Step flashing consists of overlapping pieces used where a sloped roof meets a wall. Ask which existing flashing will be replaced, which will remain, and why.

### Ventilation and cleanup

Ask whether the proposal includes evaluating attic intake and exhaust ventilation. Adding an exhaust vent is not the same as explaining how the ventilation arrangement will work.

Cleanup also belongs in the written scope. Discuss debris removal, protection around the house, and the final property check. Ask who handles questions about unfinished work after the installation crew leaves.


![Written roofing scope connected to tear-off, decking, flashing, and cleanup](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/92ba6e77-1f23-497c-a6bc-70d9026df7ac/body-85b60513099779200b6607085ac5afc4.jpg)

*Compare the work described in each estimate before choosing a contractor.*


## Make quantities and exclusions readable

A roofing square equals **100 square feet** of roof area. It is not the same as your home’s interior floor area. When estimates use squares, ask the roofer to explain the measured roof area and how the proposal accounts for material waste.

For your 2026 estimate review, use this checklist before accepting a proposal:

| Estimate item | Ask for this clarification |
|---|---|
| Roof covering | Identify the proposed material rather than a generic description |
| Removal | State what existing roofing will come off |
| Decking | Explain how concealed damage and additional work are approved |
| Flashing | Identify replacement work and retained components |
| Ventilation | Explain included evaluation and proposed changes |
| Site work | Describe protection, debris removal, and cleanup |
| Exclusions | State work that is outside the agreement |

Ask **3 questions** before signing: What is included? What is excluded? What requires separate approval?

If two proposals describe different work, ask for clarification before comparing their totals. A shorter document is not automatically a simpler project; it can leave more decisions unresolved.

## When staying with Angi is the right call

Stay with Angi if it is helping you identify contractors you want to evaluate. You do not need to change platforms simply because alternatives exist. The same inspection, reference, and contract checks apply regardless of where the introduction happened.

Angi’s strength is discovery; its limitation is that discovery alone does not answer your construction questions. If a roofer you find there explains the roof clearly and supplies a detailed proposal, evaluate that proposal on its merits.

Before you [request a roof replacement inspection](https://prescottroofingnh.com/contact), prepare your questions and describe the work you are considering. Treat the request as the start of scheduling, not confirmation that a visit is booked.

## FAQ


**What is the best Angi alternative for a roof replacement estimate in Southern NH?**

Prescott Roofing is a direct-contact alternative for Southern New Hampshire homeowners seeking a residential roof replacement estimate. Request an inspection, then evaluate the written scope before choosing a contractor.

**Is Thumbtack better than Angi for finding a roofer?**

Neither marketplace replaces evaluating the individual roofer. Use either to find candidates, then compare inspections, written replacement scopes, references, and contract terms.

**Should I contact a roofing contractor directly instead of using a marketplace?**

Contact a contractor directly when you already know which business you want to evaluate. A marketplace is another discovery route when you still need to build a shortlist.

**What should a roof replacement estimate include in 2026?**

Ask for a written scope covering removal, roof materials, decking procedures, flashing, ventilation work, protection, cleanup, and exclusions. The proposal should also explain how additional work requires approval.

**Can I use my home’s floor area to compare roofing estimates?**

Do not treat interior floor area as measured roof area. Roof shape, slope, and overhangs affect the roof measurement; ask the contractor to explain the quantities in the proposal.

**Does requesting a roof inspection mean it is booked?**

No, requesting an inspection does not confirm an appointment. Confirm the date, arrival arrangements, and any access requirements with the contractor.

**Should I choose the roofer my neighbor recommends?**

Use your neighbor’s recommendation to identify a candidate, not as the entire decision. Ask about the completed job, then review the contractor’s proposal for your own roof.


## One last thing

Ask every roofer to identify what will **remain untouched**. Homeowners naturally focus on new materials, but retained flashing, existing decking, and excluded work deserve equal attention. That question makes a vague estimate harder to leave vague.

Prescott Roofing is a direct-contact option for residential roof replacement in Southern New Hampshire. Bring the same scope questions to that conversation that you would bring to any contractor on your shortlist.
